title: 2 Kings Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 22.

questions.question: How old was Josiah when he began to reign?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:1 states that Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign.

questions.question: What was the name of Josiah's mother?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:1 mentions that Josiah's mother's name was Jedidah.

questions.question: How many years did Josiah reign in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:1 records that Josiah reigned thirty and one years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: Josiah turned aside to the right or to the left in his ways.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:2 states Josiah turned not aside to the right hand or to the left.

questions.question: In Josiah's eighteenth year, whom did the king send to the house of the LORD?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:3 records that Josiah sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, the scribe, to the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What was Shaphan instructed to have Hilkiah the priest do?
options: Sum the silver brought into the house of the LORD
Repair the breaches in the house of the LORD
Read the book of the law
questions.correctAnswer: Sum the silver brought into the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:4 says Shaphan was told to go to Hilkiah to sum the silver brought into the house of the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: The money gathered for repairing the house of the LORD was given to the overseers to pay carpenters, builders, and masons.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:5-6 explains that the money was delivered to overseers to pay carpenters, builders, and masons to repair the house.

questions.question: Which group was NOT mentioned as receiving money to repair the house of the LORD?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:6 lists carpenters, builders, and masons, but not priests, as recipients of money to repair the house.

questions.question: True or False: A reckoning was made with the workers for the money delivered to repair the house.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:7 states there was no reckoning made with the workers because they dealt faithfully.

questions.question: What did Hilkiah the high priest find in the house of the LORD?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:8 explains that Hilkiah found the book of the law in the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What did Shaphan do with the book Hilkiah gave him?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:10 records that Shaphan read the book before the king.

questions.question: Sequence Question: In 2 Kings 22, which event came first?
options: Josiah sends Shaphan to the house of the LORD
Hilkiah finds the book of the law
Shaphan reads the book to the king
The house of the LORD is repaired
questions.correctAnswer: Josiah sends Shaphan to the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:3 shows Josiah first sent Shaphan; then Hilkiah found the book (v.8), and later Shaphan read it to the king (v.10). Repairs are mentioned earlier but as an ongoing work.

questions.question: True or False: Josiah did what was right in the sight of the LORD and followed all the ways of David.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:2 clearly states Josiah did that which was right and walked in all the ways of David.

questions.question: Who gathered the silver brought into the house of the LORD?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:4 states the keepers of the door gathered the silver for the house of the LORD.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the money gathered and delivered to the overseers of the house of the LORD?
options: To repair breaches in the house
questions.correctAnswer: To repair breaches in the house
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:5 explains the money was given to those overseeing the work to repair breaches in the house of the LORD.

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who found the book of the law in the house of the LORD?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:8 states that Hilkiah the high priest found the book of the law in the house of the LORD and gave it to Shaphan the scribe.

questions.question: What did Shaphan do after receiving the book of the law from Hilkiah?
options: He gave it to the king's mother
questions.explanation: According to 2 Kings 22:8 and 22:10, Shaphan read the book of the law before the king after Hilkiah gave it to him.

questions.question: How did the king react when he heard the words of the book of the law?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:11 shows that when the king heard the words of the book of the law, he rent his clothes, showing his distress and repentance.

questions.question: Who were commanded by the king to enquire of the LORD about the words of the book found?
options: Hilkiah, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asahiah
questions.correctAnswer: Hilkiah, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asahiah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:12 records that the king commanded Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asahiah to inquire of the LORD concerning the words of the book.

questions.question: What was the reason for the LORD’s wrath kindled against Judah according to the book?
options: Because their fathers did not obey the words of the book
Because the king was too young
Because the temple was fully repaired
questions.correctAnswer: Because their fathers did not obey the words of the book
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:13 explains the LORD’s wrath was kindled because their fathers did not hearken to the words of the book to do all that was written concerning them.

questions.question: Where did Hilkiah and the others go to inquire of the LORD?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:14 states that Hilkiah, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asahiah went to Huldah the prophetess to inquire of the LORD.

questions.question: What was Huldah’s relationship or position mentioned in the chapter?
options: She was the wife of Shallum, keeper of the wardrobe, and a prophetess dwelling in Jerusalem
She was a priestess in the temple
She was a scribe in the king’s court
questions.correctAnswer: She was the wife of Shallum, keeper of the wardrobe, and a prophetess dwelling in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:14 describes Huldah as the wife of Shallum, keeper of the wardrobe, and a prophetess living in Jerusalem in the college.

questions.question: What did Huldah prophesy would happen to the place and its inhabitants because of their disobedience?
options: Evil would come upon this place and its inhabitants
They would become rulers over other nations
They would be spared from all harm
questions.correctAnswer: Evil would come upon this place and its inhabitants
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 22:16-17, Huldah prophesied that evil would be brought upon the place and its inhabitants because they forsook God and burned incense to other gods.

questions.question: How does this chapter teach us about humility and repentance through King Josiah's actions?
options: He ignored the book of the law and continued as before
He humbly rent his clothes and wept after hearing the law
He punished Hilkiah for finding the book
He immediately declared war on other nations
questions.correctAnswer: He humbly rent his clothes and wept after hearing the law
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:11 and 22:19 show Josiah’s humility and repentance as he rent his clothes and wept before the LORD after hearing the words of the law, demonstrating sincere repentance.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 22:20 promise will happen to King Josiah because of his tender heart and humility described in verse 19?
options: He will be taken to war immediately
He will be gathered to his grave in peace and not see the evil coming upon the land
He will be made king of another nation
He will be cursed along with the people
questions.correctAnswer: He will be gathered to his grave in peace and not see the evil coming upon the land
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:19-20 explains that because Josiah humbled himself and wept, the LORD promises he will be gathered to his fathers in peace and will not see the evil coming upon the land.

questions.question: What lesson about integrity can be learned from the handling of money for repairs in the house of the LORD?
options: The money was stolen by the workers
No reckoning was made because they dealt faithfully with the money
The money was used for the king’s palace
The workers refused to accept payment
questions.correctAnswer: No reckoning was made because they dealt faithfully with the money
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:7 states that no reckoning was made of the money because the workers dealt faithfully, teaching integrity in stewardship.

questions.question: True or False: Shaphan the scribe only reported to the king about the money gathered and not about the book of the law found.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:9-10 shows that Shaphan reported to the king both about the money gathered and also read the book of the law to him.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD’s wrath was kindled against the people because they burned incense to other gods, provoking Him to anger.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:17 clearly states that the LORD’s wrath was kindled because the people forsook Him and burned incense to other gods, provoking His anger.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Kings 22:13, the king sent the men to inquire of the LORD because the book was lost and never found.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:13 explains that the king sent the men to inquire because of the great wrath of the LORD kindled against them due to not hearkening to the words of the found book, not because the book was lost.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 22:14-17 demonstrate the importance of seeking God’s guidance when confronted with difficult truths?
options: They ignored the book and continued their usual practices
They sought the prophetess Huldah to inquire of the LORD, receiving a clear message about consequences
They destroyed the book to avoid the truth
They blamed each other for the book being found
questions.correctAnswer: They sought the prophetess Huldah to inquire of the LORD, receiving a clear message about consequences
questions.explanation: Verses 14-17 show that after hearing the troubling words of the book, the king sent trusted leaders to seek God’s guidance from the prophetess Huldah, who gave a prophetic message about coming judgment, illustrating the value of seeking God in difficult times.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 22.

questions.question: Who was the prophetess that King Josiah's officials consulted about the words of the book of the law?
questions.explanation: The officials went to Huldah the prophetess to inquire of the LORD concerning the words of the book, as stated in 2 Kings 22:14.

questions.question: What was the reason God said He would bring evil upon Jerusalem and its inhabitants?
options: Because they had forsaken God and burned incense to other gods
Because they had worshiped only the LORD
Because they had built a new temple
Because they had followed all the laws perfectly
questions.correctAnswer: Because they had forsaken God and burned incense to other gods
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:17 states that the evil would come because the inhabitants forsook God and burned incense to other gods, provoking His anger.

questions.question: What was the LORD's response to King Josiah's humble and tender heart after hearing the words against Jerusalem?
options: Josiah would see the destruction of Jerusalem
Josiah would be gathered to his grave in peace
questions.correctAnswer: Josiah would be gathered to his grave in peace
questions.explanation: The LORD promised Josiah peace in death because of his humility and tears, as recorded in 2 Kings 22:19-20.

questions.question: What did King Josiah do when he heard the words of the book of the law?
questions.explanation: Upon hearing the words of the book, Josiah rent his clothes as a sign of mourning and repentance, according to 2 Kings 22:11.

questions.question: Who was the scribe that read the book of the law to King Josiah?
questions.explanation: Shaphan the scribe read the book of the law before the king as described in 2 Kings 22:10.

questions.question: What task was assigned to the carpenters, builders, and masons according to Josiah’s instructions?
options: To repair the breaches of the house of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To repair the breaches of the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Josiah ordered the repairs of the temple, assigning carpenters, builders, and masons for this work as per 2 Kings 22:6.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'wrath' (used in 2 Kings 22:17) primarily convey in this context?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'wrath' here expresses God's intense anger and impending judgment against the people for their idolatry, as seen in 2 Kings 22:17.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book famously echoes the theme of a 'book of the law' being discovered and leading to reform, paralleling 2 Kings 22?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 8 recounts the reading of the Law to the people and subsequent reforms, paralleling the discovery of the book in 2 Kings 22:8-11.

questions.question: What literary device is primarily demonstrated by the structure of the king’s reaction and God’s message in 2 Kings 22:19-20?
questions.explanation: The passage uses a chiasm structure where Josiah’s humility and God’s response form a mirrored arrangement emphasizing mercy despite judgment, as in 2 Kings 22:19-20.

questions.question: True or False: The officials who consulted Huldah included Hilkiah, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asahiah.
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:12-14 lists these individuals as those sent to inquire of the LORD through Huldah.

questions.question: True or False: The book of the law found by Hilkiah was a newly written text created during Josiah’s reign.
questions.explanation: The book of the law was an existing text found in the temple, not newly written, as described in 2 Kings 22:8.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of humility and repentance seen in Josiah’s reaction to God’s word?
questions.explanation: Luke 18:14 teaches that those who humble themselves will be exalted, echoing Josiah’s humble heart and God’s favorable response in 2 Kings 22:19.

questions.question: What was the role of the 'keeper of the wardrobe,' mentioned in connection with Huldah in 2 Kings 22:14?
options: A position responsible for royal or temple garments
A scribe who wrote the law
questions.correctAnswer: A position responsible for royal or temple garments
questions.explanation: The keeper of the wardrobe managed clothing, indicating a temple or royal administrative role, as per the cultural context in 2 Kings 22:14.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 22 reveal about the historical context of Josiah’s reign in relation to the temple?
options: The temple was in disrepair and needed restoration
The temple was newly built by Josiah
The temple was destroyed during his reign
The temple was used exclusively for idol worship
questions.correctAnswer: The temple was in disrepair and needed restoration
questions.explanation: Josiah ordered repair of the temple’s breaches, showing it was in disrepair, as in 2 Kings 22:5-6.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 22, who gave the book of the law to Shaphan the scribe?
questions.explanation: Hilkiah found the book of the law and gave it to Shaphan, as recorded in 2 Kings 22:8.

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 22:2 reveal about Josiah's personal faith and leadership?
options: He continued the idolatrous practices of his ancestors
He walked in all the way of David his father and did right in the sight of the LORD
He was indifferent to the covenant of God
He followed the counsel of foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: He walked in all the way of David his father and did right in the sight of the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:2 states that Josiah 'did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, and walked in all the way of David his father, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left,' highlighting his faithful obedience and covenantal leadership.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 22:4-6, what was the purpose of the silver collected and given to the overseers of the house of the LORD?
options: To repair the breaches of the house of the LORD by hiring carpenters, builders, and masons
questions.correctAnswer: To repair the breaches of the house of the LORD by hiring carpenters, builders, and masons
questions.explanation: Verses 4-6 describe how the silver was gathered to be given to those overseeing the house of the LORD to repair it, including paying carpenters, builders, masons, and buying timber and hewn stone for restoration.

questions.question: What theological principle is demonstrated by the statement in 2 Kings 22:7 that no accounting was made of the money because they dealt faithfully?
options: The doctrine of stewardship and integrity
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of stewardship and integrity
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:7 teaches that those entrusted with the money were faithful and trustworthy, illustrating the biblical doctrine that God calls for integrity and responsible stewardship over resources (cf. Luke 16:10).

questions.question: What significant discovery does Hilkiah the high priest report to Shaphan in 2 Kings 22:8?
options: The book of the law found in the house of the LORD
A hidden treasure under the temple
questions.correctAnswer: The book of the law found in the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 8 states that Hilkiah found the book of the law in the house of the LORD, a pivotal moment revealing God's covenant word rediscovered during Josiah's reign.

questions.question: How does Josiah respond after hearing the words of the discovered book of the law, according to 2 Kings 22:11?
options: He rejoiced and celebrated with the people
He rent his clothes in sorrow
He ordered the book to be hidden
questions.correctAnswer: He rent his clothes in sorrow
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22:11 recounts Josiah's reaction of mourning by tearing his clothes, demonstrating repentance and recognition of the seriousness of Israel's covenant disobedience (cf. Joel 2:13).

questions.question: What is the theological significance of Josiah sending a delegation to inquire of the LORD after hearing the book of the law, as stated in 2 Kings 22:12-13?
options: It shows human autonomy without reliance on God
It illustrates the necessity of seeking divine guidance and covenant renewal
It reflects political maneuvering without spiritual concern
It demonstrates rejection of the prophetic word
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the necessity of seeking divine guidance and covenant renewal
questions.explanation: Josiah’s commissioning of a group to seek the LORD’s counsel (2 Kings 22:12-13) underscores the biblical principle that true repentance and reform require divine revelation and guidance (cf. Jeremiah 29:13).

questions.question: Who did the delegation sent by Josiah consult according to 2 Kings 22:14?
questions.explanation: Verse 14 details that the delegation consulted Huldah the prophetess, indicating God's use of prophetic figures, including women, to communicate His word.

questions.question: What divine attribute is revealed in Huldah's prophecy concerning the coming evil upon Judah in 2 Kings 22:16-17?
options: God’s wrath due to covenant unfaithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: God’s wrath due to covenant unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: Verses 16-17 reveal God’s righteous wrath against Judah because they forsook Him and burned incense to other gods, demonstrating His holiness and justice in punishing covenant unfaithfulness (cf. Ezekiel 18:20).

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 22:19 illustrate God’s response to sincere repentance?
options: God listens and responds with peace to the repentant heart
God punishes immediately regardless of repentance
questions.correctAnswer: God listens and responds with peace to the repentant heart
questions.explanation: Verse 19 explains that because Josiah humbly repented and tore his clothes, God heard him, showing the gracious attribute of God who responds to genuine repentance with compassion (cf. 2 Chronicles 7:14).

questions.question: What promise does God give Josiah in 2 Kings 22:20 as a result of his humility and repentance?
options: Josiah will see the destruction of Judah
Josiah will be spared from witnessing the coming evil and die in peace
questions.correctAnswer: Josiah will be spared from witnessing the coming evil and die in peace
questions.explanation: God promises Josiah in verse 20 that he will be gathered to his grave in peace and will not see the calamity coming on Judah, showing God's mercy in judgment.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the discovery of the book of the law in 2 Kings 22:8 is a later invention to justify reforms. What does 2 Kings 22:8-10 actually teach about this event?
options: It was a fabricated story without historical basis
It was a genuine discovery that led to reading and understanding of God's covenant
It was a political ploy to increase royal power
It was a myth created to promote priestly authority
questions.correctAnswer: It was a genuine discovery that led to reading and understanding of God's covenant
questions.explanation: Verses 8-10 show Hilkiah found the book, gave it to Shaphan who read it to the king, leading to covenant renewal, indicating a genuine rediscovery of God's law with theological and historical significance (cf. Deuteronomy 31:24-26).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do 2 Kings 22:11 and 2 Kings 22:19 convey about the relationship between divine revelation and human response?
options: Divine revelation is ignored by all humans
Human response to revelation is irrelevant to God's plan
Divine revelation leads to conviction and repentance, which God graciously accepts
Human emotions are irrelevant in faith
questions.correctAnswer: Divine revelation leads to conviction and repentance, which God graciously accepts
questions.explanation: Verse 11 shows Josiah's mourning upon hearing the law, and verse 19 shows God acknowledges his humble repentance, teaching that revelation prompts conviction and God responds with grace to true repentance.

questions.question: How do 2 Kings 22:4-6 and 2 Kings 22:7 together teach about the doctrine of stewardship in the context of the temple restoration?
options: Stewardship involves careful management and faithful service without corruption
Stewardship is unimportant in spiritual matters
All funds should be used only for sacrifices
Stewardship is the king's sole responsibility
questions.correctAnswer: Stewardship involves careful management and faithful service without corruption
questions.explanation: Verses 4-6 describe the collection and use of silver for temple repair, and verse 7 emphasizes no accounting was made because the workers acted faithfully, illustrating biblical stewardship of resources (cf. 1 Corinthians 4:2).

questions.question: What does the sending of a mixed delegation including priests, scribes, and a servant in 2 Kings 22:12-14 illustrate about the communal and ecclesiastical nature of seeking God's revelation?
options: Only the king should seek God's word alone
Seeking God's word is a communal and multi-office responsibility
The king's servants have no role in spiritual matters
questions.correctAnswer: Seeking God's word is a communal and multi-office responsibility
questions.explanation: Verses 12-14 show Josiah sending priests, scribes, and servants to consult the prophetess, highlighting how God's revelation involves multiple offices and the community in ecclesiastical inquiry.

questions.question: What attribute of God is primarily demonstrated in 2 Kings 22:17 when it mentions that God's wrath shall not be quenched because of the people's idolatry?
questions.explanation: Verse 17 reveals God's wrath that will not be quenched due to idolatry, demonstrating His holiness and justice in punishing sin that violates the covenant (cf. Habakkuk 1:13).
